base_method_text.title: DiffDA: a Diffusion Model for Weather-scale Data Assimilation
base_method_text.summary:
The generation of initial conditions via accurate data assimilation is
crucial for weather forecasting and climate modeling. We propose DiffDA as a
denoising diffusion model capable of assimilating atmospheric variables using
predicted states and sparse observations. Acknowledging the similarity between
a weather forecast model and a denoising diffusion model dedicated to weather
applications, we adapt the pretrained GraphCast neural network as the backbone
of the diffusion model. Through experiments based on simulated observations
from the ERA5 reanalysis dataset, our method can produce assimilated global
atmospheric data consistent with observations at 0.25 deg (~30km) resolution
globally. This marks the highest resolution achieved by ML data assimilation
models. The experiments also show that the initial conditions assimilated from
sparse observations (less than 0.96% of gridded data) and 48-hour forecast can
be used for forecast models with a loss of lead time of at most 24 hours
compared to initial conditions from state-of-the-art data assimilation in ERA5.
This enables the application of the method to real-world applications, such as
creating reanalysis datasets with autoregressive data assimilation.
base_method_text.main_contributions: The paper introduces DiffDA, a novel machine learning method for weather-scale data assimilation using a denoising diffusion model. It achieves high-resolution data assimilation (0.25°) and demonstrates the creation of data assimilation cycles with a machine learning weather forecasting model, maintaining consistency with observations. The method adapts a pre-trained GraphCast model as its backbone.
base_method_text.methodology: The method employs a denoising diffusion probabilistic model (DDPM) conditioned on both predicted states (from GraphCast) and sparse observations. It utilizes a soft mask and interpolated observations to enhance conditioning, and adapts the GraphCast neural network as the backbone of the diffusion model. The approach leverages inpainting techniques to handle sparse observations during inference.
base_method_text.experimental_setup: The experiments use the WeatherBench2 dataset, derived from ERA5 reanalysis data, as a proxy for real-world observations. The model is trained on data from 1979 to 2015, validated on 2016 data, and tested on 2022 data. The experiments include single-step data assimilation, autoregressive data assimilation, and forecast evaluation using assimilated data as input. Root Mean Square Errors (RMSEs) are used to evaluate the accuracy of the assimilated data and forecasts.
base_method_text.limitations: The method currently supports point measurements at a single time step as observations, excluding satellite imagery and radar soundings. It also lacks quality control of the input observation data, relying on simulated observations from the ERA5 dataset.
base_method_text.future_research_directions: Future research directions include supporting broader types of observations (satellite imagery, radar soundings) and multiple time steps using loss-function-based conditioning. The authors also plan to explore adding conditioning of satellite imagery directly into the diffusion model. Investigating and embedding quality control techniques for the input observation data is another planned direction.

add_method_texts.title:
Characteristic Guidance: Non-linear Correction for Diffusion Model at
  Large Guidance Scale
add_method_texts.summary:
Popular guidance for denoising diffusion probabilistic model (DDPM) linearly
combines distinct conditional models together to provide enhanced control over
samples. However, this approach overlooks nonlinear effects that become
significant when guidance scale is large. To address this issue, we propose
characteristic guidance, a guidance method that provides first-principle
non-linear correction for classifier-free guidance. Such correction forces the
guided DDPMs to respect the Fokker-Planck (FP) equation of diffusion process,
in a way that is training-free and compatible with existing sampling methods.
Experiments show that characteristic guidance enhances semantic characteristics
of prompts and mitigate irregularities in image generation, proving effective
in diverse applications ranging from simulating magnet phase transitions to
latent space sampling.
add_method_texts.main_contributions: The paper introduces "characteristic guidance," a novel method to correct the non-linearity neglected in classifier-free guidance for denoising diffusion probabilistic models (DDPMs) at large guidance scales. The method enforces the guided DDPMs to respect the Fokker-Planck (FP) equation of the diffusion process. This approach enhances the semantic characteristics of prompts, mitigates irregularities in image generation, and is training-free and compatible with existing sampling methods.
add_method_texts.methodology: Characteristic guidance employs a non-linear correction term (∆x) to the classifier-free guidance formula, determined through a fixed-point iteration method. It leverages the method of characteristics to solve the score Fokker-Planck (FP) equation under the Harmonic ansatz, which assumes the optimal DDPM solution is harmonic. Orthogonal projection operators are used as regularization to accelerate computation.
add_method_texts.experimental_setup: The method was evaluated on conditional 2D Gaussian distributions, mixture of Gaussian distributions, simulating magnet phase transitions, CIFAR-10, ImageNet 256, and Stable Diffusion. Metrics used include Kullback–Leibler (KL) divergence, Frechet Inception Distance (FID), Inception Score (IS), negative log-likelihood (NLL), and visual inspection.
add_method_texts.limitations: The effectiveness of FID for evaluating guided DDPMs is compromised by the difference between the target conditional probabilities and marginal probabilities. The iterative computations involving neural networks to solve the non-linear correction can be slow without effective regularization.
add_method_texts.future_research_directions: Future research could focus on exploring advanced regularization techniques beyond projection to enhance the convergence rate and accelerate computation. Additionally, developing more appropriate metrics beyond FID for evaluating guided DDPMs is suggested.
